title: truss event log line
description: One line of <truss dir>/events.jsonl (rolled to events.<n>.jsonl past 3 MiB), appended by truss's hooks from 0.4.0 (truss ADR-0003). Each line is one JSON object matching this schema. Read by retro/counts.ts, which skips a line that isn't JSON or has a v it doesn't know, and counts the skips. No line holds message, prompt or report text (P8).

v.description: The line's shape. Goes up when a field is renamed or retyped.

ts.description: The engine clock, as toISOString() gives it (UTC, Z).

crew.description: The crew's name: its project manager's spawn name, as reports/<crew>/ uses it.

agent.description: The agent the event is about, by its spawn name, else its id. For spawn: the new agent (the caller is by); for stall: the idle agent; for tag: the project manager; for report: the reporting agent; for allowance-spent: the QC whose FAIL report spent the allowance.

allOf.description: Every event except the crew-level ones of truss ADR-0033 and the wave-2 kinds of contract-025 names its agent. Those (crew-decision, decision-reply, decision-ack, knowledge-commit, knowledge, escalate, resolve, notify-error, budget-hold, intake, unattended and ltc) are about a crew or the run, not an agent, and carry no agent field.

then.description: An exception raised to the inbox (contract-025 section 3). id is E-<yyyymmdd>-<6hex>; blocking says the linked crews are held until it is resolved.
An inbox item resolved (contract-025 section 3). by is who resolved it.
The client-owned notify command failed for an inbox item (fail open; contract-025 section 3). error is cut to its first 200 characters.
A budget held a start, admit or queue-next (contract-025 section 4). spentUsd is null when the spend could not be priced.
One intake run over a source (contract-025 section 6). added is how many new queue items it made, seen how many it saw.
The unattended mode went on or off (contract-025 section 7). item is the queue item the run works, or null.
A long-term cost line was found (contract-025 section 3). id is the inbox item it escalated to, or null when it did not escalate; reversal is how costly it is to undo.

What a Workflow crew's optional learning came to, recorded by factory finish from the crew result's knowledge field (truss ADR-0033), once per crew and run. items is how many learned items its members reported (a product call's item is not one); ran is whether the knowledge step ran; sourceChanges is how many non-test source files its diff added, renamed or deleted. The retro counts crews, items and steps run versus skipped from it.

A product call a crew's product-owner persona made and went on from, recorded by factory crew-decision (truss ADR-0033). id is d-<crew>-<n>; task is the member task the question came from; by is who decided.
The main session's reply to a crew's product call, recorded by factory decision-reply (truss ADR-0033). ack keeps the answer; change replaces it, and note says with what (null on an ack without one).
The crew applied these replies to its product calls and said so with factory decision-ack (truss ADR-0033). ids are the replies newly marked consumed by that call, never one already consumed.

The commit that holds a crew's knowledge step, recorded by factory knowledge-commit (truss ADR-0033). owns-check lets the docs that commit changed, and no other commit did, stand outside the crew's owns.

A crew's rework allowance is spent: its QC FAIL count passed reworkAllowance (truss ADR-0004 section 5). Written by the hooks on the project manager path and by factory finish for a Workflow crew (truss ADR-0009).
A crew agent's or a project manager's Agent call that the engine let through.

model.description: The model the call asked for, or null.

effort.description: The effort the call asked for, or null.

persona.description: The persona the stage.js member ran as (truss ADR-0032), or null. Absent on lines written before ADR-0032.

by.description: main for the PM, else the calling agent's spawn name; factory for a workflow crew factory.ts started, workflow:<run id> for an agent a stage.js run started.

then.description: A Workflow stage.js run that ended without a result, recorded by factory finish (truss ADR-0009). agent repeats crew; run is the Workflow run id (the run's transcript folder name).

The card title for a Workflow agent, recorded by factory admit --label --title before the agent starts (truss ADR-0015 Decision 6). agent repeats label; label is the agent's Workflow label; title is one line, at most 120 characters.

persona.description: The persona the agent runs as, from factory admit --persona (truss ADR-0032); factory finish copies it onto the spawn line.

high.description: True when stage.js meant the agent to run at effort high (admit --high), so the effort audit lets it through.

then.description: factory finish retired a member worktree and its branch, or a branch whose worktree was gone (truss ADR-0030). agent repeats branch; run is the Workflow run the member belonged to; worktree is its path, or null for a branch alone; archive is the ref the branch tip was kept under when the target lacked it, else null.

factory finish stopped a process the run started (or an orphan) whose cwd was inside a worktree it was retiring (truss ADR-0030). agent is the worktree's branch; signal is the one that ended it, or null when it outlived SIGKILL.

A Workflow member that returned CHECKPOINT or no report was restarted by stage.js (truss ADR-0021 Decision 5), recorded by factory finish from the run journal. agent repeats label; label is the restarted member; n counts from 1 within the chain.
The resource sampler threw, and a start went ahead anyway (fail open; truss ADR-0015). Written by factory admit, heavy or start. crew and agent are both the crew slug.

error.description: The sampler error's message, cut to its first 200 characters.

then.description: One stall or idle project manager wake, when its prompt goes out.

minutes.description: Whole minutes idle, rounded down: the number the wake's prompt shows.

then.description: A project manager's tagged message to main, or a Workflow crew's stage.js stop as factory finish records it (truss ADR-0009): then agent repeats crew and run is the Workflow run id.

One WebFetch or WebSearch call (truss ADR-0005 section 11). crew is the caller's crew slug, or main for a caller outside every crew; agent is the agent's name, or main for the main session. url (WebFetch) keeps scheme, host, port and path, with userinfo removed, each query value emptied and the fragment dropped; query (WebSearch) is cut to its first 200 characters. Written only while a plan.json exists.

One tool call refused before or as it ran (P24). crew is the caller's crew slug, or main for a caller outside every crew; agent is the agent's name, or main for the main session. source names who refused: truss (truss's own hooks), worktree-guard (Claude Code's worktree confinement for an isolated agent), classifier (the auto-mode classifier), permission (a permission rule or the person), other (another plugin's deny). category is the refusal's own reason with quoted names and paths taken out; program is a Bash command's first word and shape the kinds of part its first line holds, never the command's text. Written only while a plan.json exists.
A crew agent's final report written to its report file (not an interim stop).

marker.description: The report's leading marker, from its first non-empty line, or null.
